question: Will CDU win the most seats in the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election?
summary: Late-February polls show CDU leading Greens by a narrow margin, making the seat outcome sensitive to late shifts and the new electoral rules.
AfD vote share remains sizable and could distort seat allocation, adding risk to CDU’s lead in seats.
Historical BW patterns favor Greens in seats, and market signals, while strong for CDU, do not fully mitigate late-campaign uncertainty.
Overall, the CDU is still the most likely largest party, but the probability of CDU having the most seats is lower than the raw poll-based ensemble suggests.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and highlight credible sources of risk that could alter the seat distribution, notably the razor-thin margin and the new electoral system.
justification.adjustment: Reduced from 0.91 to 0.78 to account for late-campaign uncertainty and seat-translation risk; range 0.70–0.86 conveys the plausible spread.

forecasts.reference-class: Pre-election forecasts for Baden-Württemberg 2026 based on CDU-leading polls (Infratest dimap, INSA, Forschungsgruppe Wahlen as reported by SWR, Stuttgarter Zeitung, SWP) and market-based signals (prediction markets such as Polymarket/Polychances).

sources.claim: SWR/Infratest dimap poll around Feb 2026 shows CDU ~29%, Greens ~20%, AfD ~18-22%; CDU still leads in Baden-Württemberg 2026.
SWP summary of Infratest dimap poll: CDU 29%, AfD ~21%, Greens ~20% ( Feb 2026 ); CDU remains the largest party.
BWTrend (Oct 2025) shows AfD ahead of Greens; CDU ~29% in the same period.
Wikipedia summarises multiple polls through Feb 2026: CDU ~27-29%, Greens ~20-25%, AfD ~19-22%, depending on poll.
DPA summary (Oct 2025) indicates CDU ~29%, AfD ~22%, Greens ~20%.
Prediction market assigns CDU ~93% probability of winning the most seats.
Grok predicts CDU leads roughly 29% vs Greens 21-23%, with Greens in second; market signals support CDU as largest party.
Infratest dimap poll (Feb 25–26, 2026) shows CDU at 28%, Greens at 27%; seat projection around CDU 37 seats vs Greens 35 in a 120-seat Landtag.
Forschungsgruppe Wahlen poll (Feb 26, 2026) shows CDU at 27%, Greens at 25%; seat projection CDU 37 seats vs Greens 35.

The 2026 Baden-Württemberg state election is scheduled for March 8, 2026; polls indicate CDU leading Greens in the contest with CDU generally in the high-20s and Greens in the mid-20s to high-20s range.
DPA report summarized by Yahoo News: CDU ahead of Greens (around 28% vs 27% in Infratest dimap) in late February 2026.
SWP summary of late-2025/early-2026 surveys showing Greens gaining, CDU stabil, and CDU ahead in several polls.
INSA and Infratest dimap polling cited in a 2025 article indicating CDU ahead of Greens in Baden-Württemberg in that period.
Infratest dimap poll (ARD) shows CDU 28.0%, Greens 27.0%, AfD 18.0%, SPD 7.0%, FDP 6.0%, Linke 5.5%, Others 8.5%.
SWP summarizes a late-February poll indicating the race is tight with CDU around 28% and Greens around 27%, reflecting a narrow lead for the CDU in ARD data.
INSA poll (Feb 17–23, 2026) shows CDU 28%, Greens 22% in Baden-Württemberg.
Aggregated Baden-Württemberg 2026 polls show CDU around 28–29% and Greens around 22–27% depending on the pollster.
Past Baden-Württemberg Landtag results (2021): Greens 32.6% (58 seats) vs CDU 24.1% (42 seats); indicates Greens have previously won the most seats under the prior system.

causal-factors.name: Sustained CDU polling lead in late February 2026
causal-factors.rationale: Late-February polls show CDU around 28% and Greens around 27%, which supports CDU as the largest party and thus increases the probability of CDU winning the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Prediction-market signal CDU will win the most seats
causal-factors.rationale: Markets such as Polymarket assign a high probability to CDU leading in seat count, elevating the odds beyond polls alone.

causal-factors.name: Historically Greens-led seat totals in BW
causal-factors.rationale: BW has trended toward Greens-leading seat shares since 2011, which acts as a counterbalance against a CDU-led outcome.

causal-factors.name: Greens closing the vote-gap window in late campaign
causal-factors.rationale: Insa and other polls show Greens narrowing CDU lead, raising the risk CDU loses the top-seat position.

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system dynamics and seat allocation
causal-factors.rationale: The 120-seat Landtag system can produce non-proportional seat outcomes with small swings, creating modest uncertainty about CDU being the largest seat holder.

causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead in late-February surveys
causal-factors.rationale: Late-February polls show CDU ahead of Greens by about 1-4 percentage points, sustaining CDU as the largest party ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/de/baden-wuerttemberg/wahlumfragen/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/landtagswahl?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Greens closing the margin / gaining ground in polls
causal-factors.rationale: Greens are closing the gap in late-February polls, reducing CDU's lead ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/baden-wuerttemberg/opinion-polls/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/state-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: AfD vote share remains sizable and could siphon votes from major parties
causal-factors.rationale: AfD remains a sizable share around 18–22%, potentially siphoning votes from both CDU and Greens and altering the seat distribution ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/de/baden-wuerttemberg/wahlumfragen/infratest-dimap-2026-02-25/landtagswahl?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Turnout dynamics and urban/rural vote patterns affecting seat allocation
causal-factors.rationale: Turnout shifts could disproportionately affect urban-leaning Greens, narrowing CDU's seat lead in the Landtag ([de.wikipedia.org](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landtagswahl_in_Baden-W%C3%BCrttemberg_2026?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Introduction of a new dual-vote electoral system and its uncertainty for seat translation
causal-factors.rationale: The 2026 Baden-Württemberg election uses a revised system that changes how votes translate into seats, adding uncertainty in whether current vote shares map to seats in the same way as under the previous rules ([de.wikipedia.org](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landtagswahl_in_Baden-W%C3%BCrttemberg_2026?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Narrow CDU lead in late-Feb polls (Infratest dimap, Feb 25–26, 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: CDU at 28% and Greens at 27% with only a 1 percentage point gap increases sensitivity to late shifts that could flip who wins the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Greens gaining ground in late-Feb polls (Infratest dimap and FGW indicators)
causal-factors.rationale: Greens around 25–27% in several polls tighten the race and threaten CDU's seat lead, raising the risk of CDU losing the top-seat position.

causal-factors.name: Seat-projection signals CDU remains largest party but with a modest lead
causal-factors.rationale: Projections commonly show CDU ahead (e.g., roughly 36–37 seats vs Greens in the high 20s to mid-30s), sustaining CDU as the largest party.

causal-factors.name: Prediction-market signals CDU will win the most seats (high implied probability)
causal-factors.rationale: Markets such as Polymarket indicate a very high probability for CDU to win the most seats, reinforcing the CDU-leaning baseline.

synthesis: The CDU remains the most plausible winner in seats, but a razor-thin margin, new seat-translation rules, and AfD dynamics introduce meaningful risk. Calibrated probability reflects these uncertainties with a center around 0.78 and a 0.70–0.86 range.
